name: South Dakota

context: SD 329: No-till leaves residue on the soil surface year around to reduce sheet, rill and wind erosion.
SD 340: Cover crops are used to reduce sheet, rill and wind erosion; time establishment to protect soil in critical erosion periods.
cover_rules: SD 340: For wind erosion use erosion prediction technology to set the surface and canopy cover needed from the cover crop. No fall tillage.
SD 340: Select cover crops with the physical characteristics needed to give adequate erosion protection.
residue: SD 329: Keep a minimum of 60 percent residue cover (flat) on the soil surface whenever it is not covered by living plant canopy.
SD 345: Reduced till crop interval STIR value must be no greater than 80; for wind erosion set standing residue height and row direction with prediction technology.
SD 329: Do not burn residue; distribute residues uniformly over the whole field.
barriers: SD 589: Trap strips at least 15 feet wide if vegetation or stubble is 1 foot or more in height during erosion periods; at least 25 feet if under 1 foot.
SD 603: Herbaceous wind barriers need minimum expected height of 1.5 feet and porosity of 40 to 50 percent; spacing no more than 10 times barrier height.
SD 585: Stripcrop strips run perpendicular to prevailing wind; set strip width with wind erosion prediction technology.
windbreak: SD 380: Protected zone is 10H on the leeward side and 2H on the windward side; plant perpendicular to the erosive wind.
SD 380: Choose species taller than the crop; set the interval between windbreaks with erosion prediction technology.
roughening: SD 588: Crosswind ridges: spacing no more than four times ridge height, orientation within 45 degrees of perpendicular to erosive wind.
SD 588: Ridges suit loamy and clayey soils; not well adapted on sandy soils.
grazing: SD 528: Plan grazing to keep adequate ground cover from canopy, litter and trampled residue to reduce wind and water erosion.
SD 528: Minimize grazing impact on areas with high soil erosion potential.
drought: SD 528: Prepare written contingencies for episodic disturbances such as drought, and avoid grazing when conditions are not appropriate.
seeding: SD 550: Calculate seeding rates on a pure live seed (PLS) basis; select species that give cover to control wind and water erosion.
